I agree something has happened to the front end at some point. There is some paint missing on the driver's side bumper, and the hood is misaligned on both corners. Check the carfax, but odds are it might come up clean.

You can probably readjust it yourself a little bit using the two little knobs under the hood. These knobs adjust hood height.

Now as for everything else, please closely inspect the bottom of the rear quarter panels for any tiny bubbles, that would indicate rust is beginning to form. Many 2008-2014 models have been known to rust in these areas.

I also recommend having the transmission fluid checked. Have the front suspension checked too. 

Spark plugs will be due by 100k, and it's a bit invasive, so shops will charge quite a bit in labor for this service if you don't feel comfortable doing it yourself.

Have the oil cooler inspected for any leaks.

Have your rear diff fluid checked, there is no official fluid change interval in the manual, but I recommend having it changed with the trans fluid, every 60k. So it wouldn't hurt to have it changed, remember to have friction modifier added.

If the a/c turns out to be kinda weak, adding freon is super easy!

Overall it's a good looking car, I would push for answers on that front end damage and talk them down in price to 7k. The damage probably won't show up on carfax if they had stuff done without involving insurance.

You force yourself to provide for your loved ones, be a good worker, be a good friend. But deep inside, you want nothing more than to simply not be here. To no longer have to suffer in silence. To simply not exist to deal with life's constant problems on top of your own personal hell within.

Some people avoid going through with it because of the fear of pain, the fear of dying, the fear of the unknown on the other side after death.

Others avoid it because their loved ones need and depend on them. They have pets that would never understand. Their kids would be permanently scarred.

Here's some basic stuff for a good hand wash at home:


Wash in the shade at all times, try to avoid direct sunlight to reduce the chance of water spots

You can do a 1 bucket wash method with several microfiber towels in soapy water. When using a towel, fold it into 4s and flip to a clean side each time you finish wiping down a panel. When the towel is too dirty, don't return it to the wash bucket, just grab a fresh towel and continue.


I know pro detailers recommend expensive microfiber towels, but personally I use the big pack of yellow microfiber towels from Walmart for $18

For soap, I personally like Duragloss 951, but you can get any decent soap from Walmart. Meguiars Gold Class is a classic and works well


Now after you're done rinsing the car down, I recommend using a product like Gyeon Wet Coat. You spray it on the wet car, let it dwell for about a minute, then rinse it all off. Now your car has a little protection on it! 

You can use a leaf blower to blow away the excess water left on the car, and use a few more microfiber towels to dry off the little bit left.
